obligation: G054 (transfer matrix coverage) + G055 (first universal rule) + G057 (search policy)
status: COMPLETE -- 7 architecture families, both designated falsifiers survived
claim: CROSS-LAYER SUBSPACE ALIGNMENT SPLITS BY RESIDUAL-STREAM SIDE. Organs that READ the residual stream align above a matched random null; organs that read a per-layer space and WRITE into the residual sit at chance. Within every specimen scored, every reader beats every writer.
first_form_was_wrong: The hypothesis born on Qwen3-0.6B said the split was input DIMENSION -- organs whose in_dim equals hidden_size align, others do not. Three of the next four specimens refute that classifier: o_proj's input is n_heads*head_dim which usually EQUALS hidden_size, so ModernBERT attn.Wo (1.14x), BitNet o_proj (1.00x) and LFM2 out_proj (0.98x) are all 'in_dim == hidden' and all at chance. The surviving form is about WHICH OBJECT the input is, not how big it is.
method: Weights only, no forward pass, no tokenizer. Top-64 right singular subspaces per layer; overlap_r(i,j) = ||V_i^T V_j||_F^2 / r over all layer pairs; null MEASURED from random orthonormal r-frames of identical shape, not assumed to be r/d. Randomized SVD. 28-109s per specimen on CPU.
families: natively ternary, never trained in a continuous weight space (BitNet b1.58-2B)
mechanism: The residual stream is ONE OBJECT every layer reads, so it carries a preferred basis and its readers partially align to it. A writer's input -- the MLP intermediate, the head concatenation, the conv output -- is constructed fresh inside each layer and shared with nothing, so there is no common basis for it to align to. This predicts the split on any architecture with a residual stream, including ones with no attention.

THE ARITHMETIC THAT MAKES IT UNPAYABLE.finding: Alignment strength is IRRELEVANT to whether shared-basis factorisation pays. Sharing one input basis V (d x R) across n same-role layers of shape (m, d) costs d*R + n*m*R against a dense n*m*d, so break-even is R* = n*m*d/(d + n*m), which approaches d as n*m grows. Every realistic body has n*m >> d.
THE ARITHMETIC THAT MAKES IT UNPAYABLE.consequence: A 5.6x-aligned organ still needs 86-99% of its input basis to survive just to break even. The alignment is real and strong and buys nothing in this form, because the arithmetic never had room for it.
THE ARITHMETIC THAT MAKES IT UNPAYABLE.search_policy_G057: Shared-input-basis cross-layer factorisation can now be ruled out on any specimen by ONE LINE of arithmetic, before any SVD, any calibration set, or any GPU. This is the first rule in the base that removes an experiment class from future specimens rather than describing one that was run.

what_the_alignment_might_still_buy: Only forms whose cost is NOT governed by n*m/(d + n*m): a shared codebook or dictionary (cost independent of layer count), cross-layer weight PREDICTION (no basis stored at all), or as a prior that narrows an activation-aware search. Those are separate obligations, not this one.
notable: BitNet -- natively ternary, never trained in a continuous weight space -- shows among the STRONGEST reader alignment measured (4.45-5.62x), and mamba3, with no attention mechanism at all, is comparable (5.26-5.38x). Neither the training representation nor the mixing mechanism weakens the effect, which is what a residual-stream explanation predicts.

unmeasured_not_negative.state-spaces--mamba3-mimo-1.5b: first pass reported ZERO roles -- which reads exactly like 'this family has no cross-layer structure' and was actually 'the prober only opens safetensors and this ships a .bin'. Closed the format gap and re-ran; it then gave among the strongest reader alignments measured.

falsifier: a specimen whose writers align as well as its readers

designated_falsifiers.chosen_before_running: RWKV7 and a diffusion LM, because neither has a conventional attention block and RWKV replaces the whole mixing mechanism. If the law were an artefact of attention it would break here.
designated_falsifiers.RWKV7: HOLDS with the widest margin measured: readers 5.00-7.51x, writers 1.05-2.23x. Its ffn.value at 2.23x is the only writer materially above chance in the whole population and is still less than half the smallest reader.

classification_caveat: Roles are classified by NAME informed by architecture, not by a mechanical suffix rule, and RWKV is why: it names BOTH a reader and a writer 'value'. att.value takes the residual (d=4096) and ffn.value is the FFN's down-projection (d=16384). A bare-suffix classifier gets one of them wrong. The earlier dimension-based classifier (in_dim == hidden_size) is wrong for a different reason and was refuted by this same transfer test.
cost: 28-544s CPU per specimen, weights only, no forward pass, no tokenizer, no GPU
